page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.2xlarge is an x86_64 server instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. It features 8 virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core using dedicated CPU allocation. The system includes 32 GB of RAM, yielding 4 GB per virtual CPU, along with 479 GB of local SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Hardware-level vector instruction support includes AVX, AVX2, and AVX-512 extensions.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate average multi-core and memory performance across standard tests, including a PassMark CPU score of 8,286.39 and Geekbench 5 scores of 1,187 single-core and 4,479 multi-core. Single-core performance tests such as stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression fall into the lower quartile. In application-focused metrics, the instance achieves 6.88 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 6.92 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, though performance degrades in heavy machine learning workloads such as 7B parameter LLM inference.

With bundled local SSD storage and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance offers cost efficiency for workloads requiring direct fast disk access without requiring separate storage volume attachments. Tradeoffs include modest single-core execution speed and constrained network throughput compared to larger compute-focused instances. The hardware configuration makes it suitable for relational and NoSQL databases, caching layers, web serving, and general enterprise workloads requiring localized storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.2xlarge is a cloud server instance featuring 8 vCPUs on 4 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 32 GB of RAM and 479 GB of local SSD storage. Designed with dedicated CPU allocation, the server maintains a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate balanced multi-core CPU and memory throughput, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,479 and 6.88 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside lower single-core execution speeds in stress-ng and gzip testing. The inclusion of integrated local SSD storage provides efficient read/write performance for database management and caching layers without external drive attachments. Tradeoffs involve reduced single-threaded throughput and modest LLM execution capacity, making the instance best suited for web serving, database hosting, and general application workloads requiring local storage access.
